newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga to give rebates for blackout.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga to give rebates for blackout.

text.p: Malaysian utility firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd will give a 10 percent rebate to consumers affected by the peninsula-wide August 3 blackout, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Wednesday.
The national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying that consumers will get a five percent rebate in their December 1996 bills, and another five percent in their January 1997 bills.
The rebates will cost Tenaga 70 million ringgit, Moggie told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting.
The rebate was agreed upon by the cabinet, he said.

The government had previously said it was considering giving consumers some form of compensation for the 12-15 hour blackout over peninsula Malaysia. But recent statements from government officials including Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad noted that other countries do not pay compensation for blackouts.
A total of 4.2 million consumers are expected to benefit from the rebates in their December and January bills, Moggie said.
Tenaga stock, which was up 30 cents before the news and rose as much as 55 cents on Wednesday, closed unchanged at 9.30 ringgit.
Moggie said the rebate should not be mistaken for compensation by Tenaga Nasional and that it was only a "one-off" ex-gratia payment to those affected by the August 3 outage.
Earlier, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad told reporters at Parliament House that the decision should not be made a precedent.

"We acknowledge that everywhere in the world there is no responsibility attached to public utility (firms) for such incidents. But the government has a slightly different stand," Bernama quoted him as saying.
Moggie said that only consumers registered with the utility company on August 3 would be eligible for the payment.
The "goodwill" payment should not be interpreted as admitting liability on Tenaga Nasional's part, he said, adding that the rebate would not apply to blackouts prior to the August incident.
Malaysia had a similar massive blackout four years ago.
